NDT training in the Midwest: how it works

Short answer: NDT training for the Midwest runs in three parts. You study the theory online at your own pace on the Atlantis portal, with an ASNT Level III answering your questions; you practice in the Practical NDT browser simulator; and you complete hands-on work and the practical examination at the employer's plant or shop. The employer then certifies you under a written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A.

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in the Midwest, and nobody needs to travel to one: the company's offices are in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India, and everything a candidate does before the practical happens online. Course access opens the moment you enroll, at any point in the year, so there is no start date to wait for. The courses are written and supported by an ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT with more than 11 years of international field experience.

This guide has two readers in mind. One is an individual in Gary, Toledo, Milwaukee or the Twin Cities who wants to get into NDT, add a method or move up a level. The other is an employer, whether an inspection company, a fabrication shop or a plant, that has to train, examine and certify a crew without pulling people off the floor for weeks.

Where NDT technicians work across the Midwest

Inspection work in the Midwest follows heavy industry, and most of it sits close to the Great Lakes and the big rivers.

Steel on the south shore of Lake Michigan. U.S. Steel's Gary Works and the Cleveland-Cliffs mills at Burns Harbor and Indiana Harbor are a short drive apart, and BP's Whiting refinery shares the same shoreline. Mill maintenance generates steady work in UT thickness and weld examination, MT on crane runways, hooks and lifting gear, and VT on structural repairs. Local detail: NDT training in Whiting and NDT training in Chicago.

Chicago and northern Illinois. ExxonMobil's Joliet refinery and Citgo's Lemont refinery anchor the in-service side, with API inspection programs for vessels, piping and tanks. Constellation's nuclear stations at Byron, Braidwood, LaSalle and Dresden bring refueling outages, and Illinois operates more reactors than any other state.

Detroit and Michigan. The auto industry still drives a large share of the state's castings, forgings and tooling, which keeps MT, PT and UT busy on parts before they ship. Marathon's Detroit refinery adds in-service work, DTE's Fermi 2 plant near Monroe adds nuclear outages, and the effort to restart the Palisades plant in southwest Michigan, which still had no restart date in mid-2026, shows how unsettled the generating fleet is. See NDT training in Detroit.

Cleveland, Toledo and northern Ohio. Cleveland-Cliffs' Cleveland Works, the refineries around Toledo, and Vistra's Perry and Davis-Besse nuclear plants give northern Ohio mill, refinery and outage work within a couple of hours' drive. See NDT training in Cleveland and NDT training in Toledo.

Indianapolis and central Indiana. Rolls-Royce builds and supports aircraft engines in Indianapolis and Allison Transmission is headquartered there, so precision components bring PT, MT and ET work under customer specifications alongside the general fabrication base. See NDT training in Indianapolis.

Milwaukee and Wisconsin. Foundries, forge shops and heavy-equipment builders make Milwaukee a castings-and-forgings market, with UT on forgings and MT on welded frames. NextEra's Point Beach plant on the lakeshore adds outage work. See NDT training in Milwaukee.

Minneapolis–St. Paul and the upper Midwest. Flint Hills Resources' Pine Bend refinery and Marathon's St. Paul Park refinery, Xcel Energy's Prairie Island and Monticello nuclear plants, and the Enbridge crude pipeline system crossing Minnesota toward Superior, Wisconsin combine refinery, outage and pipeline work. See NDT training in Minneapolis and NDT training in Duluth.

St. Louis and the river crossing. Boeing builds military aircraft in St. Louis, Phillips 66 runs the Wood River refinery across the Mississippi in Roxana, Illinois, and Ameren's Callaway plant sits west of the city. The river is also a regulatory line for radiography, as the licensing section below explains. See NDT training in St. Louis.

Which NDT methods and levels Midwest employers ask for

Most Midwest hiring centers on the four workhorse methods, VT, MT, PT and UT, at Level II, because that is the level that can set up equipment, perform the examination and accept or reject against the code. The table shows how the governing documents change by sector.

SectorMethods most requestedCodes that govern acceptance
Structural steel fabricationVT, MT, UTAWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code; AWS D1.5 for bridge girders
Pressure vessels and boilers (new construction)VT, PT, MT, UT, RTASME Section VIII and Section I, with examination methods in ASME Section V
Refineries and chemical plants (in service)UT thickness, VT, MT, PTAPI 510, API 570 and API 653 inspection codes; ASME B31.3 for process piping
Steel mills and heavy maintenanceUT, MT, VTOwner specifications, ASME B30 for lifting equipment, AWS D1.1 for structural repairs
Castings and forgingsMT, PT, UTCustomer drawings and specifications; ASTM practices such as A388 for forgings and E709 for MT
Nuclear plantsUT, VT, PT, MT, ETASME Section XI for in-service inspection, plus the plant's nuclear quality program
Fossil and gas-fired generationUT, MT, PT, VTASME Section I and ASME B31.1 power piping
PipelinesVT, UT, MTAPI 1104 for welding; 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195 for operators

Eddy current (ET) matters wherever there are heat-exchanger and condenser tubes, which means refineries and power plants. Radiography (RT) remains part of new-construction work, but it carries a licensing layer the other methods do not. For a newcomer, the practical sequence is VT plus MT or PT, then UT, which takes longest to learn and opens the most doors in this region. Begin with NDT Level 1 training, move to NDT Level 2 training, and look at ultrasonic testing training once the surface methods feel routine.

How NDT certification works across state lines in the Midwest

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the employer certifies the technician, and the certificate is valid only for that employer. A course, including ours, certifies no one. The employer's written practice sets the training hours, experience hours, examinations and vision checks, and the employer's Level III signs the record. That has a practical consequence in a region where a technician can work at a Gary fabricator one year and an Ohio refinery contractor the next: when you change employer, the new employer recertifies you under its own written practice.

Recertifying is not starting over. A new employer can accept your documented classroom hours and supervised experience if the records are complete, then give you its own general, specific and practical examinations. Keep a personal copy of your training certificates, an experience log signed by your supervisors, and your vision test results. State borders make no difference to SNT-TC-1A; the written practice belongs to the company, not to Indiana, Illinois or Ohio. Our SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker shows the hours each level calls for.

If you want a credential that stays with you rather than with the employer, ASNT's central certifications, ASNT NDT Level II and ASNT NDT Level III, are examined and issued by ASNT itself and renewed with ASNT. Employers still decide whether to accept them for their work, but they carry over when you move. Atlantis prepares candidates for those examinations; ASNT runs them and issues the certificates. The ASNT certification guide compares the routes.

Sector overlays sit on top of the written practice. Nuclear in-service inspection follows ASME Section XI, and ultrasonic examiners there also need performance demonstration qualification under Section XI Appendix VIII, so an SNT-TC-1A certificate is the entry point rather than the finish. Aerospace engine work flows customer requirements down to the shop, and Nadcap AC7114 audits check them. Pipeline operators add operator qualification programs for covered tasks under federal pipeline safety rules. Each overlay is the employer's to meet, and each one assumes the SNT-TC-1A foundation is solid.

Radiography licensing across the Midwest's states

RT training teaches the method. It licenses nobody. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed by the state radiation control program in an Agreement State, or by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission where the state has no agreement, and the license is held by the employer, not the technician. A radiographer must also complete radiation safety training and pass a radiographer certification examination run by a recognized certifying entity, arranged under the employer's license.

The Midwest is a patchwork. Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio and Wisconsin are Agreement States. Indiana joined them when its agreement with the NRC took effect on September 30, 2026, making it the 41st Agreement State, so radiography licensing for most work in Indiana now runs through the state rather than the NRC. Michigan and Missouri have no agreement, and the NRC licenses radiography there directly. A crew based in St. Louis therefore deals with the NRC on the Missouri bank and the Illinois program on the other side of the river, and a Gary contractor working into Michigan crosses from one system to the other.

When a licensed crew works temporarily in another jurisdiction, the license holder files for reciprocity before the job, and work inside areas of exclusive federal jurisdiction can fall to the NRC even within an Agreement State. None of this is the technician's paperwork, but it decides which jobs an RT trainee can join. If you want RT, look for an employer that already holds a radiography license, then take radiographic testing training for the method knowledge.

Choosing an NDT training provider in the Midwest

The region has more ways into NDT than most. Community and technical colleges run NDT certificate and associate programs with lab time on real equipment. Private NDT schools offer intensive method courses. Many fabricators, mills and inspection companies train new hires on the job and send them to outside theory courses as needed. And self-paced online theory, paired with a practical at the employer, suits people who already have a job or a job offer.

Whichever route you weigh, ask the same questions:

  • Does the course follow the body of knowledge and the recommended training hours in SNT-TC-1A for the method and level you need?
  • Who answers technical questions, and what level and methods does that person hold?
  • How will you get hands-on time on real equipment and real parts, and who examines your practical?
  • Will your employer, or the employer you hope to join, accept the course hours under its written practice? Ask its Level III before you pay for anything.
  • What records do you leave with, and do they show hours and topics clearly enough for an auditor?

Colleges and schools suit someone starting from zero who wants structured lab time before applying for jobs. The online route suits a working technician adding a method, a welder moving into inspection at the same shop, or an employer that wants the theory done without a week away from production. Our NDT training courses and NDT training in the USA pages set out how it works, and the published US course fees are on this page.

Training an NDT crew across several Midwest sites

Employers with crews spread across Indiana, Illinois and Ohio usually want two things: one standard for everybody and as little travel as possible. Atlantis delivers training on-site at the employer's facility, on its own equipment, procedures and parts, with theory taken online beforehand so the time on-site goes to hands-on work and the practical examination.

The anchor is one written practice. If each site has drifted into its own habits, the certification records will not survive a customer audit, and technicians moving between sites will be examined against different rules. A single company written practice built on SNT-TC-1A, with site-specific procedures underneath it, fixes that. We can review an existing document or write one with you through our NDT written practice development service, and set up the examinations and records through SNT-TC-1A training program setup.

Plan around the work calendar. Mills and refineries schedule outages and turnarounds months ahead, and that is when experience hours build fastest, so train beforehand and let the outage supply the supervised hours. Tell us the methods, levels, headcount and sites, and we reply within one business day.

Practice before your NDT practical

The practical examination tests setup, calibration and documentation as much as flaw detection. The Practical NDT simulator runs in a browser, on a PC or in VR, and lets a Midwest trainee rehearse each step of an examination before touching the employer's equipment. It supports training; it does not replace supervised experience, the practical examination or employer certification.

For the written side, the free NDT practice tests cover Level II questions in UT, PAUT, TOFD, ET, RT, MT, PT and VT, with explanations, so you can find weak topics before the general and specific examinations.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in the Midwest

More general answers are in the NDT training FAQ.

How long does NDT training take in the Midwest?

The classroom part depends on the method and level: VT, MT and PT need the fewest hours, UT and RT the most, and the employer's written practice sets the final numbers. Because the theory is self-paced, a working technician can finish one method's theory in a few weeks of evenings. Certification takes longer, because SNT-TC-1A also calls for supervised experience hours before the employer can certify you.

Can I do NDT training online from Chicago, Detroit or Cleveland?

Yes, the theory. You study online at your own pace with an ASNT Level III answering questions, and the hands-on training and practical examination happen in person at your employer's facility. Our online NDT training page explains how the two parts fit together.

Is there NDT training near me in the Midwest?

Atlantis has no walk-in location anywhere in the region, so the honest answer for an employer is "at your own facility," and for an individual it is "online, with the practical at the employer you work for or are joining." Colleges and schools in the larger metros offer classroom routes if you want lab time before you have a job.

Which NDT method should I learn to start with?

In this region, MT or PT plus VT, then UT. Fabrication shops and mills use the surface methods every day, they are quicker to learn, and they get you into experience hours sooner. UT then opens refinery, mill and pressure-equipment work.

I am moving from Indiana to Ohio. Does my NDT certification move with me?

Not automatically. SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the employer, so your new employer recertifies you under its written practice. Bring your training certificates, signed experience records and vision test results, and the process is usually re-examination rather than retraining. ASNT central certification is the portable alternative.

How do I become an NDT Level III in the Midwest?

Most Level IIIs come up through years as a Level II and then pass ASNT's Basic and method examinations, which need documented experience before you can sit them. Our self-paced ASNT Level III training prepares you for those examinations; ASNT examines and certifies.

Do you offer AWS CWI training in the Midwest?

Yes. The six-day AWS CWI exam prep course runs in three formats: corporate at your facility, online, or one-to-one, online or in person. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification. Local pages cover AWS CWI training in Chicago, Detroit and Columbus.
